questions.q: Which Multiplier type improves decisions by opening the floor to debate and weighing every option?
a: The Debate Maker
The Liberator
The Investor
The Talent Magnet
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists the Debate Maker among the five Multiplier types, creating an open environment where all options are considered.

questions.q: What do Diminishers do to the people on their team?
a: They drain enthusiasm and leave people feeling inferior
They magnify strengths and share credit generously
They stretch people with ambitious challenges
They hand over ownership and hold people accountable
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Diminishers as draining enthusiasm and skills while employees feel inferior and unfulfilled.

questions.q: What does the summary advise when a Diminisher criticizes you?
a: Pause, cool off, then return with a new solution
Confront them publicly and demand an apology
Lay low and wait for them to leave the company
Quit quickly and look for a better boss
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends taking time to calm down instead of reacting fast, citing a leader at Apple who regrouped after criticism.

questions.q: How can an employee turn the tables on a difficult boss?
a: By acting as a Multiplier toward that boss
By copying the boss's controlling habits
By escalating every conflict to HR
By withholding information until asked
questions.why: Lesson 2 says an employee can become a Multiplier toward their manager, directing the boss's attention to their expertise.

questions.q: What first step does the summary suggest for a leader with Diminisher tendencies?
a: Choose one strength to improve and test their assumptions
Try to become excellent at every part of the job
Wait for the team to point out the weaknesses
Replace the weakest members of the team
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests picking a single strength to work on, then testing your assumptions against the five Multiplier types.
